result.summary:
Independently read docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md and docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md in full (not CODE-DESIGNER's/DATA-DESIGNER's result.summary), plus both handoffs, requirements.yaml's REQ-031 entry (issue #34), security-invariants.md S1/S9, and the REQ-019.md/REQ-030.md precedents this design cites.

Checks that PASS:
- All 7 ACs map to a concrete, non-deferred design element (Sec8 of REQ-031.md, Sec7 of the schema doc); no 'TBD'/deferral language anywhere in either artefact (the only 'placeholder' hits are the decisions/0002-authorized placeholder-copy convention, not a deferred design decision).
- Props/types fully specified: FeedbackRecord, FeedbackFlowStep, FeedbackJobCandidate, RegistrationFeedbackContext, UserFeedbackState, and every function signature in Sec2-Sec6 are fully typed.
- No design-system token references anywhere (Sec9 correctly states this is a bot/Telegram surface with no visual component -- confirmed against tokens.css scope; nothing invented).
- No implementation code: only TypeScript signatures + prose/comment description of behavior and SQL shape, consistent with the established REQ-014/016/019/025 schema-doc convention (the schema doc's 'expected statement shape' SQL is explicitly labeled illustrative, for BACKEND-DEV/REVIEWER to confirm the generated migration against, not authored SQL).
- AC2 (DB-constraint dedup): traced to a real DB object -- Sec1.1 of the schema doc puts a UNIQUE index (uq_feedback_registration_id) directly on feedback.registration_id, which a raw duplicate INSERT collides with regardless of application code (23505 unique_violation) -- genuinely satisfies AC2's own stated verification method, not merely an application-level dedup.
- AC4 (exactly one T+24h reminder, ever): traced to REQ-025's existing notification_ledger UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) constraint, reused unchanged, with feedback_reminder as its own distinct NotificationKind (Sec5.1) -- a T+48h re-run's ledger insert for the same (registration_id, 'feedback_reminder') collides with the T+24h row and no-ops, independent of whether Sec5.3's catch-up window even re-selects the candidate at T+48h.
- AC5 (asked once, gate is asked_at not the answer): re-verified directly against the design text, not the producer's summary -- Sec2.7's determineFeedbackFlowStep and Sec0.3's own resolution both gate on `broadcastOptInAskedAt !== null`, never on `broadcastOptIn`'s value; Sec0.3 explicitly states this also covers the prior-yes case ('there is exactly one suppression condition, "already asked," regardless of the answer'). Sound and explicit, not assumed.
- AC6 (no Talk entity): explicit textual scope-boundary statement present (REQ-031.md Sec8's AC6 row: 'explicitly scoped out in the requirement text itself... and restated here as a deliberate, stated omission rather than a silent one'), not merely an absence of a talks table.
- S1 (consent precedes storage): REQ-031.md Sec1.1 explicitly states, not merely assumes, why feedback collection needs no new store-my-data consent -- 'every feedback respondent is already a known, consented member (they hold an admitted registration with a non-null checked_in_at -- S1 is already satisfied for them long before this flow starts)'. Sound: S1 gates storage on consent_pd_at having been given once (at onboarding, REQ-014/019), not per-datum-type; a checked-in admitted registrant already carries that consent. The broadcast-opt-in ('message me') consent is kept in its own home throughout (Sec0.3/Sec2.6: writeBroadcastOptInAnswer is the design's own stated ONLY writer of broadcast_opt_in/broadcast_opt_in_asked_at), never conflated with consent_pd_at or publish_consent, matching S1's three-consents-one-home table.
- REQ-019-vs-REQ-030 precedent departure (Sec1.1): reasoning re-derived and confirmed sound against REQ-031's actual constraints -- checked directly that REQ-030's two triggering conditions (S1 write-before-consent ban; callback_data's 64-byte cap unable to carry three free-text fields) genuinely do not hold for REQ-031 (every respondent already consented+admitted+checked-in; every callback_data payload here (Sec3.2/Sec3.3) is computed and shown to fit well inside 64 bytes). DB-derived resumability is the correct choice, not an unexamined default.
- DATA-DESIGNER's three MINOR open questions (S13 anonymization scope for the three free-text columns; no CHECK on topic_votes shape; no CHECK forbidding value+skipped=true) are appropriately non-blocking: each mirrors an identical, already-accepted precedent in REQ-019-schema.md for the same class of column, none is forced by an acceptance criterion, and none conceals a mechanism this requirement's ACs actually depend on.

CHECK THAT FAILS -- the force_reply/ref-line reply-disambiguation mechanism (REQ-031.md Sec1.2, Sec3.1, Sec6.3) does not actually deliver the guarantee its own text claims, and the specific edge case named in this gate's task (replying to a DIFFERENT, older message than the current force_reply prompt -- something Telegram explicitly permits) is not correctly handled:

- The 'Feedback ref: <registrationId>' line (Sec3.1) encodes ONLY the registration id -- it does not identify WHICH of the three optional fields (liked/improve/topicVotes) the specific prompt it is attached to was asking about.
- Sec6.3's generic text-reply handler (steps 2-3, 7-8) re-extracts only the registrationId from whatever message was replied to, then derives the CURRENTLY-expected field fresh from the database (Sec2.7), and writes the reply's text to THAT field -- with no check that the message actually replied to is the one currently expecting an answer.
- Concrete failing walkthrough: the `liked` prompt is sent (force_reply, ref line = registrationId); the respondent answers it, so the `improve` prompt is now sent (Sec2.2's own ordering); the respondent later scrolls back and replies to the OLD, already-answered `liked` message instead of the current `improve` message (Telegram allows this; Sec6.5 itself relies on old force_reply prompts staying repliable indefinitely) -- Sec6.3 step 7 derives the current step as `improve` (since `liked` is already resolved), step 8's gate only excludes `nps`/non-field steps (both fail to catch this case: field is `improve`, a valid text-answerable field), and step 11 writes the reply's text as the ANSWER TO `improve`, silently, even though the respondent replied to the `liked` prompt.
- This directly contradicts Sec6.3 step 8's own stated claim that 'a stale reply to an already-superseded prompt is silently ignored, same convention as every other stale-tap case in this design' -- that claim is FALSE for exactly this case (a reply to a superseded prompt whose own field differs from, but is a sibling text-answerable field of, the currently-expected one). The design asserts a guarantee it does not actually implement.
- This is not a hypothetical corner case: STORY-DETAILS D1's own respect-the-respondent framing (already cited elsewhere in this design) is undermined by silently storing a person's `liked` correction/afterthought as their `improve` answer with no error and no way for them to discover the misattribution.
- Not raised anywhere in Sec10's five named open questions, despite Sec10 otherwise being conscientious about naming exactly this class of unresolved edge case.

Per Step 1b's own rule ('FAIL immediately on any check failure -- no partial credit'), this single gap is sufficient for FAIL even though every other check passes.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md Sec1.2/Sec3.1/Sec6.3: the ref-line disambiguation mechanism identifies only the registration a reply belongs to, not the specific field the replied-to prompt was asking about. A reply to a superseded (but not-yet-forgotten, still-repliable per Sec6.5) prompt for a DIFFERENT field than the one currently expected gets silently written to the CURRENTLY-expected field instead of being recognized as stale -- contradicting Sec6.3 step 8's own claim that stale replies are 'silently ignored.' REQUIRED FIX: either (a) have formatFeedbackTextPrompt (Sec3.1) additionally encode the specific field the prompt is for (e.g. a second ref-line token, 'Feedback field: <field>'), and add a check in the Sec6.3 handler (before step 8's existing gate) that the parsed field matches the field the replied-to message was actually for, treating a mismatch as a no-op exactly like every other stale-tap case in this design; or (b) if silently reattributing such a reply to whatever field is currently pending is judged the intended, acceptable behavior, state that explicitly as a considered design decision with reasoning (why misattribution is an acceptable tradeoff, or why the scenario cannot actually arise) -- it must not remain an unstated side effect of a mechanism whose own text asserts a stronger guarantee than it delivers.

result.next_action: Rework CODE-DESIGNER: resolve the MAJOR issue above in docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md (Sec1.2/Sec3.1/Sec6.3, and update Sec10's open-questions list if the resolution leaves anything genuinely open), then re-route to CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR for a fresh Step 1b pass. No change to docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md is required by this issue -- DATA-DESIGNER's artefact passes every check independently and does not need rework unless CODE-DESIGNER's fix requires a new column (e.g. option (a) above needs no schema change, since the field name would live in the existing force_reply message text, not a new stored column).
